project: MoerEngine ConsoleVariable Bootstrap And In-Editor Console
goal: Introduce a dedicated ConsoleVariable.ini startup override layer for engine CVar initial values, provide a bottom-left resident console with input and live engine logs, and expose a hotkey-driven expanded console page without keeping the current hidden or cycle-mode behavior as the main UX.

already_exists: Editor already creates ConsoleSystem as an overlay in Editor::Run.
ConsoleSystem already has command input, command history, autocomplete, a bottom-left inline window, and a separate windowed console page.
The grave accent key is already wired through WindowInput and GLFW key mapping.
ConsoleSystem already parses `help`, `cvar list`, `<path> ?`, and `<path> <value>` commands.
blocking_gaps: LogSystem::PollConsoleLogs currently always returns false and ClearConsoleLogs is a no-op, so the existing console cannot actually show engine logs.
All current TCVar registrations live inside ConsoleSystem.cpp, so they do not exist during Engine::Init and cannot be overridden from startup config.
CVarSystem only supports Register, Find, and GetAll. It has no startup override loading, no file import, and no persistence layer.
ConfigManager only loads MoerEngine.toml. There is no ConsoleVariable.ini discovery or override phase.
Runtime configuration files are loaded from the executable directory, and CMake currently only copies MoerEngine.toml plus assets, so a new ConsoleVariable.ini would not be deployed automatically.
Current console UX is a three-state cycle Hidden -> Inline -> Windowed. That does not match the requested always-on resident console plus hotkey-open interactive page model.
design_pressure: The requested feature is not mainly an ImGui problem. The real ownership issue is that CVar registration and CVar override load order are wrong today.
If CVar definitions remain editor-local statics, ConsoleVariable.ini will only ever be a late runtime patch instead of initial-value override.
If LogSystem keeps no in-memory ring or queue, the resident console will always be visually present but functionally empty.

design_constraints: ConsoleVariable.ini is a separate config layer from MoerEngine.toml and only overrides registered CVar initial values. It must not be folded into GlobalConfig TOML parsing.
CVar registration must be available before ConsoleVariable.ini is applied. CVar ownership belongs to the runtime subsystem that actually consumes the value, not to ConsoleSystem UI code.
ConsoleVariable.ini loading should be optional. If the file does not exist, engine defaults remain valid and startup continues.
The resident bottom-left console is the default editor UX. The hotkey opens or focuses an expanded console page; it should not cycle through hidden, inline, and windowed states as the main path.
The resident console output must show real engine logs via LogSystem in-memory buffering, not ad-hoc polling from stdout or file tailing.

Validation must use existing repository scripts only. If interactive console behavior later needs stronger verification, extend existing editor smoke coverage rather than adding a new primary test wrapper.

proposed_file_contract.location: Executable working directory next to MoerEngine.toml.
proposed_file_contract.status: Optional override file copied to target/bin/<Config>/ during build.
proposed_file_contract.parse_rule: Unknown CVar names log a warning and are skipped. Type mismatch logs an error and leaves the default value unchanged.

checkpoints.title: Move CVar ownership out of ConsoleSystem and make startup registration deterministic
must_be_true_after: CVar definitions no longer depend on constructing ConsoleSystem in Editor::Run.
Each CVar is declared near the runtime or editor subsystem that owns the underlying value.
Engine startup can enumerate and override CVar values before those values are first consumed.
ConsoleSystem becomes a consumer of the CVar registry instead of the owner of engine configuration state.

checkpoints.title: Add ConsoleVariable.ini startup override loading
must_be_true_after: ConfigManager or an adjacent startup-owned config path loads ConsoleVariable.ini after CVar registration and before runtime systems consume overridden values.
Overrides are applied through the same typed CVar parsing path used by the runtime console command executor.
Startup override loading reports missing file, unknown keys, and parse failures through LogSystem with explicit messages.
ConsoleVariable.ini is copied into the executable output directory together with MoerEngine.toml.

checkpoints.title: Implement real in-memory engine log buffering for console consumption
must_be_true_after: LogSystem keeps a bounded in-memory queue or ring of ConsoleLogEntry records.
PollConsoleLogs returns real incremental log entries instead of always returning false.
ClearConsoleLogs clears the in-memory console buffer deterministically.
Resident and expanded console windows display actual engine logs from the same source of truth.

checkpoints.title: Replace cycle-mode console UX with resident panel plus hotkey-driven expanded page
must_be_true_after: A bottom-left console panel is always present in the editor main viewport.
The resident panel contains one input field and a log/output panel above it.
Hotkey behavior opens, closes, or focuses an expanded console page instead of cycling Hidden -> Inline -> Windowed.
Keyboard capture and camera-input blocking rules remain explicit and do not interfere with normal editor control when the expanded page is not focused.

checkpoints.title: Validate deployment and editor startup behavior through existing scripts
must_be_true_after: The editor still boots through the existing repository smoke path after adding ConsoleVariable.ini copy and console UI changes.
No new primary validation script is introduced for the console feature.
If later interaction coverage is needed, it is added to existing PowerShell-driven editor smoke coverage rather than a parallel script family.
The documentation for this feature clearly states that current repository scripts only give startup smoke coverage, not full hotkey interaction automation.

validation: This checkpoint file is design-only and does not require a build by itself.
When implementation starts, run powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\testscripts\test_all.ps1 as the existing editor startup smoke path.
If implementation touches RHI-facing CVar consumers, also run powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\testscripts\test_rhi_translate.ps1 before the full aggregate script.
Current repository scripts do not automate console hotkey interaction or log-window assertions; that gap should be stated explicitly until existing PowerShell coverage is extended.
